title: 28.2.2 Some Swarm services are not discoverable over DNS
body: After upgrading our two Docker Swarm environments, external requests to containers stopped working. Docker Engine 28.1.1 works, while 28.2.2 returns 504 Gateway Timeout; I also tried 28.2.1 without success. The same 28.2.2 version works in our standalone Docker environments. For example, `curl -vvv https://<my host>:443/my-api-path/actuator/health` returns 504 instead of the expected 200. The working and broken Swarm environments also have many differences in their iptables rules.

symptoms_visible: After upgrading our Swarm environments to Docker 28.2.2, requests to the published HTTPS endpoints return 504 Gateway Timeout instead of 200.
Our Swarm environment works on 28.1.1, and our standalone Docker environments work on 28.2.2.
N0.label: N0 Swarm gateway timeouts reported

symptoms_visible: Requests through Traefik time out, but the health check succeeds when it curls the application on localhost inside its container.
The service and Traefik are attached to the Docker overlay network named proxy.
N1.label: N1 overlay topology established

symptoms_visible: On Docker 28.2.2, an overlay connection may work for a while and later stop after containers restart or move.
Containers can reach a service when placed on the same node, while cross-node ping or TCP traffic to that service is dropped or times out.
Traefik receives the service task IPs but cannot connect to some of them.
N2.label: N2 intermittent cross-node overlay failure characterized

symptoms_visible: After recreating the overlay network and attaching the services again, most services became reachable, but communication later broke again.
N2_x.label: N2_x overlay recreation aftermath

symptoms_visible: In the test environment, the services remain reachable after installing Docker 28.3.0-rc.1, and the gateway timeouts no longer occur.
N3.label: N3 revert build verified

symptoms_visible: After updating to a Docker version containing the overlay-network reverts, Traefik can reach services across Swarm nodes and the public endpoints return successful responses instead of gateway timeouts.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Does the application respond from inside its own container, and do its health checks pass?
Can you curl the application directly on localhost inside the container?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. Inside the container, `curl http://localhost:8080/api-admin/actuator/health` works and the containers are marked healthy. Requests from the Docker host or a remote host through Traefik time out.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No, localhost inside the container also times out and the container is unhealthy.
The localhost health endpoint returns 200 on port 8081 instead of 8080, but external requests still time out.

question_patterns: How is the broken URL published or load-balanced?
Can you share a minimal stack configuration showing the proxy and application networking?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Traefik 3.4.1 runs above the services and routes to them using the external network named `proxy`. The application joins that network and tells Traefik to use its port 8080.

question_patterns: What kind of network is `proxy`, and how was it created?
Is the external `proxy` network actually a Docker overlay network?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. It is created by our Traefik stack with `name: proxy`, `driver: overlay`, and subnet `192.168.220.0/22`. Traefik is configured with `--providers.swarm.network=proxy`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No, `proxy` is a third-party network plugin and is not created by Docker's overlay driver.

question_patterns: Which iptables backend is used in each environment?
What differences are visible in the headers of the two `iptables-save` outputs?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The broken environment's output says `iptables-save v1.8.9 (nf_tables)`, while the working environment's output says `iptables-save v1.8.9` without that marker.

question_patterns: Apart from Docker and the iptables backend, what differs between the hosts?
Are the operating system, kernel, and host configuration otherwise the same?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Apart from the Docker versions, the VMs are identical: the same Debian 12 and kernel version, managed the same way with Puppet.

edges.comment: The reporter first established that the application itself was healthy and then clarified that the supposedly external network was a Docker-managed Swarm overlay network used by Traefik.

question_patterns: Does networking fail immediately, after some time, or after a node or service changes state?
Do container restarts or moves between nodes trigger the problem?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It may work for a period and then fail. We have seen services become unreachable after a container was redeployed, restarted, or moved to another node; other moved services can remain reachable.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It fails deterministically from the first packet after every daemon start, without any service restart, redeployment, or node movement.
The delay varies from minutes to hours, but the same intermittent failure follows service restarts or moves.

question_patterns: Can affected containers communicate when they are placed on the same node?
Is the failure limited to cross-node overlay traffic?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: When I constrain the client container to the same worker as the target service, it can connect. From another worker, ping and TCP connections to the same overlay service can fail or be dropped.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Same-node communication fails exactly like cross-node traffic, including direct connections to the task IP.

question_patterns: Does Traefik receive the service task addresses, or is service discovery returning no targets?
Can you tell whether the timeout occurs after Traefik has learned the container IP?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Traefik gets the correct IP addresses for the containers, but it cannot reach the affected ones. The application logs do not show those requests arriving.

question_patterns: Is NetworkManager, dnsmasq, or another host network manager controlling the Docker interfaces?
What does networkctl report for the Docker interfaces?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: We have neither NetworkManager nor netscript installed. On the nodes using netplan, `networkctl` reports all Docker interfaces as unmanaged.

edges.comment: Reports from several affected Swarm operators are folded into one simulated user side. Together they establish intermittent cross-node overlay loss after service state changes, while task addresses remain known and same-node traffic can work.

solution.intent: Recreate the affected overlay network and reattach or redeploy all services to restore connectivity.
solution.concrete_example: Remove and recreate the Traefik overlay network, attach the services to the new network, and scale them back up.

edges.comment: An affected operator recreated the overlay network and initially restored most services, but communication eventually failed again. This is only a temporary reset, not the fix.

question_patterns: Could you install the candidate build that carries the pending overlay fix in a test environment and repeat your Swarm connectivity tests?
Please test the release candidate with the same Traefik and cross-node overlay workload and tell me what you observe.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: We have now deployed v28.3.0-rc.1 in our testing environment and confirmed that it solves the problem for us; the services are reachable again through the proxy. We await the official v28.3.0 release before deploying to our production environment.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same services still become unreachable and Traefik still returns gateway timeouts on v28.3.0-rc.1.
The release candidate restores connectivity in a smaller test Swarm with fewer workers, using the same overlay topology.

edges.comment: A separate affected operator tested the 28.3.0 release candidate; that operator is folded into the simulated user side. The answer reports only the observed build result, while linking it to the reverted 28.2 overlay changes remains engineer-side inference.

solution.intent: Replace the affected 28.2.x or 25.0.11 engine with a fixed Docker 28.3.x build that reverts the regressing Swarm overlay-network changes; use 28.1.1 only as a temporary rollback, then verify cross-node service connectivity.
solution.concrete_example: The regression is in the overlay-network fixes and refactoring included in 28.2.x. Install Docker 28.3.0 or later, where those changes are reverted by moby/moby#50169. If an immediate workaround is needed, remain on 28.1.1. After updating, retest Traefik routes and direct cross-node overlay connections before declaring the cluster healthy.
solution.inference_hint: Maintainers inferred from the 28.1.1/28.2.x boundary, the cross-node overlay observations, and the successful 28.3.0-rc.1 test that overlay-network fixes and refactoring introduced in 28.2.x were responsible. They could not reproduce or narrow the issue to one precise internal mechanism, so an answer should not invent a more specific DNS, IP-exhaustion, iptables, or endpoint-database cause.

edges.comment: The technical resolution was moby/moby#50169, which reverted the suspect overlay-network changes for 28.3.0. Docker 25.0.11 was also reported affected through #50005. Release scheduling itself is not scored.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify this as a Docker Swarm overlay-network regression introduced by the networking fixes/refactoring in 28.2.x, grounded in the 28.1.1 versus 28.2.x behavior, intermittent cross-node failures, known task IPs, and successful 28.3.0-rc.1 test.
Must recommend Docker 28.3.0 or later containing the overlay-network reverts; rollback to 28.1.1 is acceptable only as a temporary workaround.
Must not present recreating the overlay network as the fix, because it restored connectivity only temporarily before the failure returned.
Must not settle on NetworkManager, the iptables legacy-versus-nft difference, application health, or a standalone-Docker problem as the root cause.
Must not invent a narrower mechanism such as DNS-only failure or IP exhaustion; maintainers reverted the suspect overlay changes because the precise regression could not be reproduced or isolated.
Must have the user verify Traefik and cross-node overlay connectivity on a build containing the reverts before treating the issue as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced production infrastructure operator who manages multiple Docker Swarm environments, Traefik stacks, custom address pools, iptables output, and staged upgrades; additional affected Swarm operators are folded into the same simulated user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and practical, with detailed configuration snippets and production observations; willing to test builds and compare environments, but initially describes the symptom broadly and supplies more precise topology only when asked.
